bullets.title: TSMC Q2 Blowout: Revenue $40.2B, Gross Margin 67.7%, EPS $4.31 — All Above Estimates
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 revenue of $40.2B (+33.7% YoY, top of guidance), gross margin 67.7% (above 65.5-67.5% guided range), operating margin 60.3% vs 56.5-58.5% guide, and EPS of $4.31 vs $3.77 est. Net profit of NT$706.56B hit an all-time high, up 77.4% YoY. Chairman C.C. Wei called AI demand 'so robust' we are 'witnessing the birth of a new industry.'

bullets.title: TSMC Raises 2026 Capex to $60-64B; Next 3 Years Will Be 'Even More' Than Prior 3
bullets.body: TSMC raised 2026 capex guidance from 'above $56B' to $60-64B. CFO guided that next 3-year capex will exceed the already-elevated prior 3-year period. The company also announced an additional $100B U.S. investment (N2 process and advanced packaging in Arizona) and plans for four additional Arizona fabs contingent on demand.

bullets.title: TSMC Q3 2026 Guidance Beats: $44.6-45.8B Revenue, 65-67% Gross Margin
bullets.body: TSMC guided Q3 2026 revenue at $44.6-45.8B (+12% QoQ, +37% YoY midpoint) vs $43.11B consensus, gross margin 65-67% vs 65.9% est, operating margin 56-58%. Chairman Wei expects strong Q3 demand for leading-edge AI chips; consumer electronics softer on high prices.

bullets.title: TSMC: Demand-Supply Gap 'Very Big,' AI Demand Seen Robust Through 2030
bullets.body: Chairman C.C. Wei confirmed the demand-supply gap is 'very big' and larger than the memory industry situation. TSMC sees robust demand trend continuing through 2030, is taking steps to avoid excess inventory, and sees AI adoption having broad impact across all industries. No fixed timeline for additional U.S. investment.

bullets.title: TSMC Global Expansion: 3 New 3nm Fabs, A14 Node on Track for 2028 Mass Production
bullets.body: TSMC plans three additional 3nm fabs (Taiwan, Arizona, Japan) and 13 advanced semiconductor/packaging facilities in Taiwan. A14 technology development is on track with strong HPC/smartphone demand; A13/A12 extensions target 2029. Arizona expansion pace tied to market demand signals.

bullets.title: TSMC Welcomes Intel EMIB as Competitive Flexibility; 18A Yields Jump to 85%
bullets.body: TSMC Chairman Wei said Intel's EMIB packaging competition provides market flexibility that could share loading from TSMC and benefit its front-end wafer growth. Separately, Intel 18A yields reportedly improved to ~85% from 65% last quarter, still below TSMC N2 (~90%) but above Samsung.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Japan Momentum: 27,500 Rubin Chips, Robotics, Bank AI Deployments
bullets.body: Japan plans to buy 27,500 Nvidia Rubin chips for robot AI; NVIDIA announced Japanese enterprises and banks (Mizuho, SMFG, MUFG NICOS, Rakuten) deploying Nemotron models and Agent Toolkit. NVIDIA also launched Jetson Thor T3000/T2000 for mainstream robotics and expanded Toyota physical AI collaboration. GB300 NVL72 claims 25x performance-per-watt vs Hopper.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Shrinks Robotics Chip 50% With Thor T3000/T2000; Groq 3 Racks to Ship H2 2026
bullets.body: NVIDIA's new Jetson Thor T3000 and T2000 modules halve chip size without performance loss, targeting humanoid robots and edge AI for mass-market expansion. Separately, Nvidia Groq 3 server racks (256 LPUs, 32 compute trays) expected to begin shipping H2 2026.

bullets.title: Amazon Ramping AWS Custom Chips to 2.4M Trainium3 Units in 2026; Positive for Taiwan Supply Chain
bullets.body: At AWS Summit Taipei 2026, Amazon showcased Trainium3, Inferentia, and Graviton chips with Trainium3 already shipping and targeting 2.4M units in 2026, 3.4M in 2027. The ramp is described as a strong positive signal for Taiwan chip supply chain partners.

bullets.title: Big Tech Capex Crosses $700B in 2026, ~3x Prior Run-Rate; Mag 7 Up 2.3% vs Broader Market
bullets.body: Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft combined capex for 2026 exceeds $700B, roughly 3x three years prior. On Wednesday, the Mag 7 gained 2.3% while the average S&P 500 stock fell 0.4%, extending the familiar mega-cap divergence.

bullets.title: AAPL Hits All-Time High, Approaching $5T Market Cap; Exploring Chip Acquisitions
bullets.body: Apple hit a new all-time high on Wednesday and is described as 'within striking distance' of a $5T valuation, which would make it only the second company to reach that milestone. The Information reports Apple is actively seeking chip company acquisitions to bolster server chip development.

bullets.title: Microsoft Security Overhaul: 8 Execs Replaced, Hundreds of Cuts in Security Group
bullets.body: Microsoft's new security chief Hayete Gallot replaced at least eight executives who reported to former boss Charlie Bell and cut several hundred employees from the security group to force an AI-driven overhaul. Separately, Microsoft Xbox cut 379 jobs at ZeniMax/Bethesda.

bullets.title: Tesla: Robotaxi Fleet Growing Exponentially; Bears Cite Volume Collapse and Transparency Issues
bullets.body: One bullish account notes Tesla's robotaxi fleet is growing exponentially 13 months post-launch. Bears counter that TSLA trading volume in dollars has declined since the Nov. 2024 Elon/Trump win, implying declining exit liquidity, and criticize a cancelled lower-cost vehicle program (April 2024, pulled 6 weeks later) with no public announcement.

bullets.title: Nokia Launches Nvidia-Powered AI-RAN Platform; ERIC Earnings Raise Cost Pass-Through Concerns for NOK
bullets.body: Nokia announced an AI-RAN platform powered by Nvidia. Separately, Ericsson's earnings raised concerns about component cost pass-throughs to customers, which a fintwit account flagged as relevant read-through for Nokia at current levels.

bullets.title: Netflix Reports Tonight; Analyst Asks Whether Monetization Can Offset Engagement Plateau
bullets.body: Netflix reports Q2 earnings after market close Thursday. One analyst frames the key question as whether Netflix can sustain revenue growth through monetization strategies as user engagement may be plateauing.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Sector Down 16% From June Highs; Asian Tech Rout Hits SK Hynix -9%, KOSPI -7%
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks have entered a technical correction, falling 16% from June all-time highs and approaching bear market territory. Asian markets saw a broad tech rout with SK Hynix down >9% and Seoul's KOSPI plunging 7% (triggering circuit breakers) following South Korea's first rate hike since early 2023.

bullets.title: Nasdaq 100 Futures Extend to Session Lows at -0.6%; 1%+ Daily Swings in 20 of Last 26 Days
bullets.body: Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.6% to session lows in pre-market. The QQQ has moved 1% or more in 20 of the last 26 trading days — a pattern that has historically only occurred during Covid, the 2022 bear market, the 2008 financial crisis, and the dot-com bubble.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Bond Cover Ratios Fell from ~5x to <2x; Terminal Value Debate Intensifies
bullets.body: Hyperscaler bond cover ratios declined from nearly 5x in February 2026 to below 2x in July, signaling weakening bond investor appetite for hyperscaler debt. One fintwit account argues the 'dirty secret' is that the AI invention erased hyperscalers' previous terminal values and current capex is an attempt to recover and exceed it.

bullets.title: Meta Faces Court Challenge to Block July 22 Layoffs; Tech Down 8% From June Highs
bullets.body: Meta faces a preliminary injunction request from plaintiffs seeking to block layoffs starting July 22. Separately, one fintwit account contextualizes the broad tech selloff: the sector is down 8% from June highs but gained +24.9% in 2025 YTD and +24.9% in 2024.

bullets.title: COHR/LITE: Analyst Flags UHP Laser CPO Challenges; GPU CPO Scaling 'Not Ramping'
bullets.body: One analyst flags that UHP lasers for co-packaged optics (CPO) require understanding of high-power laser physics and plans future coverage of COHR and LITE. A separate account claims GPU CPO scaling is not ramping and is delayed from earlier expectations.
